title: Mechanisms Underlying the Greater Efficacy of Robot-Assisted Gait Rehabilitation Versus Conventional Therapy Combined With Botulinum Toxin Injection of the Triceps Surae in Individuals With Chronic Post-Stroke Impairments
official: Mechanisms Underlying the Greater Efficacy of Robot-Assisted Gait Rehabilitation Versus Conventional Therapy Combined With Botulinum Toxin Injection of the Triceps Surae in Individuals With Chronic Post-Stroke Impairments
summary:
Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability in adults. Many people who have had a stroke continue to experience difficulty walking because of muscle weakness and spasticity, which can limit their mobility and quality of life.

Botulinum toxin injections are commonly used to reduce spasticity in specific muscles, such as the calf muscles. Rehabilitation is then used to improve walking ability. Robot-assisted gait rehabilitation allows patients to practice walking intensively and repeatedly, with assistance adjusted to their needs. Previous research from our team has shown that robot-assisted gait rehabilitation may improve walking ability more than conventional physical therapy when combined with botulinum toxin injections.

The purpose of this study is to better understand why robot-assisted gait rehabilitation may be more effective than conventional gait rehabilitation after botulinum toxin treatment in people with chronic stroke. The study will examine changes in walking patterns, muscle activity, and brain activity during and after rehabilitation. Brain activity and brain connections will be assessed using non-invasive methods, including functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

The study may help identify how the brain and body adapt to rehabilitation and may contribute to developing more personalized rehabilitation programs for people living with long-term effects of stroke.
conditions: Stroke (6 Months or More After Onset)

interventions.name: Combined Functional Near-infrared Spectroscopy and Electroencephalography System

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults with hemiparesis.
* Affiliated with a national or public health insurance system.
* Able and willing to provide written informed consent after receiving information about the purpose, procedures, and potential risks of the study.
* At least 6 months after a unilateral stroke.
* Presence of triceps surae spasticity causing impaired gait and treatment with botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) as part of routine care, with a stable dose for at least 2 treatment cycles.
* Able to walk for 6 minutes; walking speed \<0.8 m/s on the 10-Meter Walk Test.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Cognitive impairment preventing the participant from providing informed consent.
* Triceps surae spasticity \>3/5 on the Modified Ashworth Scale.
* Any contraindication to physical exercise, robot-assisted gait rehabilitation using the Lokomat, or MRI.
* Claustrophobia or fear of confined spaces.
* Individuals deprived of liberty by judicial or administrative decision, or under legal guardianship.
* Inability to complete all study procedures.
* Pregnancy, breastfeeding, or plans to become pregnant during the study period.
* Concurrent participation in another research study.
